summary: R0 needs the manual-vs-automation comparison defined before any live trial, and decide() needs a minimum sample that is planned, not guessed.  docs/experiments/study-design.md sets the protocol: the arms (manual control, rule-based baseline-v1, adaptive policy versions, fleet variants, PvP strategies) and their state on main; one primary metric per study, measured from snapshots so the unjournaled manual arm is comparable; every roadmap scorecard metric mapped to the existing sdk/reports field; ABBA within-account crossover or matched pairs by hull bracket, with per-bracket analysis and block splitting on hull upgrades; the intervention log; windows with a measurement-only baseline window first; and stopping rules tied to decide(). It states that no baseline data exists and lists what the owner must supply.  sdk/experiments/study.py adds a validated StudyPlan, standard-library two-proportion (Fleiss pooled, or unpooled) and two-mean sample sizes, and per_arm_min_sample / experiments_for to feed Experiment.min_sample. Because decide() adopts only on non-overlapping 95% intervals, a conventionally sized trial would adopt a real effect only about half the time; the default rule therefore sizes for decide() itself (t critical values for means, an exact binomial search over Wilson intervals for proportions). Tests check textbook values (388/385 for 0.5 vs 0.6, 63 for d = 0.5), the exact power against full enumeration, and decide() by seeded simulation. Implemented by the analyst specialist subagent in an isolated worktree, independently reviewed by the verifier subagent (APPROVE), and re-validated by the parent.
